title: Interventional effects with estimandYLL
text: intervention = "full_contrast" compares two static worlds: LEa=referenceversusLEa=exposed. \mathrm{LE}^{=\mathrm{reference}} \quad \text{versus} \quad \mathrm{LE}^{=\mathrm{exposed}}. intervention = "partial_change" compares natural observed exposure distribution policy-like partial change. example: observed-exposed people: 30% move reference, 70% stay exposed; observed-unexposed people: stay unexposed. Internally, binary stochastic intervention. subject engine forms Si*(t)=(1−pi)Sia=reference(t)+piSia=exposed(t), S_i^*(t) = (1 - p_i) S_i^{=\mathrm{reference}}(t) + p_i S_i^{=\mathrm{exposed}}(t), averages Si*(t)S_i^*(t) stated target population.

title: Interventional effects with estimandYLL
text: measure = "yll" reports LEreference−LEexposed. \mathrm{LE}_{reference} - \mathrm{LE}_{exposed}. usual years--life-lost orientation. harmful exposure tends produce positive value. measure = "life_year_change" reports clinically oriented change life expectancy stated intervention direction. ATC-like question observed-unexposed people become exposed, harmful exposure therefore gives negative value.

title: Interventional effects with estimandYLL
text: Imagine programme 20% observed-unexposed individuals become hypertensive, observed-hypertensive individuals stay hypertensive. target population explicitly observed-unexposed group.
code: library(estimandYLL) data(yll_toy)  res <- estimand_yll(   data = yll_toy,   target_population = "unexposed",   intervention = "partial_change",   change_from = "reference",   change_to = "exposed",   change_probability = 0.20,   measure = "life_year_change",   B = 50, show_progress = FALSE, use_future = FALSE,   id_var = "id", time_var = "period", event_var = "event",   exposure_var = "hypertension",   reference_level = "No", exposed_level = "Yes",   age_at_entry_var = "age",   age_start = 50, age_end = 90, age_interval = 5,   confounders_baseline = c("sex", "education_years", "bmi", "smoke_binary") )  res$summary

text: usual g-formula assumptions required: consistency counterfactual outcomes hypothesised regimes; conditional exchangeability given measured covariates; positivity chosen intervention target population; correctly specified discrete-time hazard model. text: Years life lost (YLL) counterfactual life expectancy user-specified interventions binary exposure, estimated parametric g-formula attained-age time scale. package supports: Explicit target populations: individuals, observed-exposed individuals, observed-unexposed individuals. Full exposure contrasts clinically phrased partial-change policies one main function, estimand_yll(). Conditional, observed-group YLL Poisson Royston-Parmar regression conditional_yll(). Bootstrap confidence intervals (normal-approximation percentile), optionally parallelised future. Plotting helpers marginal conditional survival curves selected YLL measure across starting ages.

title: Years of Life Lost via the G-Formula
text: main design : target_population answers “averaging ?”: "": individuals (ATE-like). "exposed": individuals observed exposed (ATT-like). "unexposed": individuals observed unexposed (ATC-like). intervention answers “exposure worlds compared?”: "full_contrast": reference versus exposed. "partial_change": natural observed distribution versus policy-like partial change, 30% observed-exposed individuals moving reference level. measure answers “result displayed?”: "yll": LE_reference - LE_exposed. "life_year_change": clinically oriented change life expectancy stated intervention direction. makes harmful ATC-like changes negative. Example: 30% smokers quit, averaged observed smokers: statistical terminology, partial_change stochastic intervention, user-facing API uses policy language. Plot helpers: plot_yll_estimate() / plot_yll() — selected estimate across starting ages. plot_marginal_survival() plot_conditional_survival() — survival curves.
code: YLL estimand = target_population + intervention + measure estimand_yll(   data = yll_toy,   id_var = "id",   time_var = "period",   event_var = "event",   exposure_var = "smoke_binary",   reference_level = "Never",   exposed_level = "Current/Ever",   age_at_entry_var = "age",   target_population = "exposed",   intervention = "partial_change",   change_from = "exposed",   change_to = "reference",   change_probability = 0.30,   measure = "life_year_change",   B = 0,   use_future = FALSE )

title: Years of Life Lost via the G-Formula
text: conditional_yll() implements regression-based observed-group comparisons similar Poisson flexible parametric Royston-Parmar approaches used YLL methods literature. separate estimand_yll(): intervention target population argument. Instead, function compares predicted remaining life expectancy reference exposed groups, optionally conditioning baseline covariates. method = "flexible_parametric" requires optional rstpm2 package.
code: res_cond <- conditional_yll(   data = yll_toy,   method = "poisson",   id_var = "id",   time_var = "period",   event_var = "event",   exposure_var = "hypertension",   reference_level = "No",   exposed_level = "Yes",   age_at_entry_var = "age",   confounders_baseline = c("sex", "education_years", "bmi", "smoke_binary"),   age_start = 50,   age_end = 90,   age_interval = 5,   B = 0 )

title: Years of Life Lost via the G-Formula
text: current implementation binary exposures. Multi-level continuous exposures yet supported. Variable entry age introduces left-truncation / delayed-entry problem current implementation address rigorously; treat results datasets variable age_at_entry_var preliminary.
